speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to better understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been present, and do you have a history of smoking or exposure to environmental irritants?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very long duration for a chronic cough, especially given the thick, yellow-green sputum you produce. Since you are a non-smoker, have you noticed any shortness of breath, wheezing, or seasonal variations in your symptoms? Also, do you have any history of heart disease or fluid retention?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Bronchitis secondary to Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD).

The clinical picture of a chronic cough with copious sputum production for over 11 years, despite a history of non-smoking, is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis or severe COPD. To confirm the extent of airway damage and rule out other causes, I need to see your imaging and lung function results.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay
REQUEST TEST: Spirometry
